payload.stem: Which statement correctly compares producer surplus and consumer surplus at a competitive equilibrium?

options.text: Producer surplus equals total revenue, while consumer surplus equals total spending minus total revenue.
options.why: Equates surplus with revenue; surplus subtracts costs or willingness to pay from the price.

options.text: Producer surplus is the difference between the price and the buyers' willingness to pay, while consumer surplus is the difference between the price and the sellers' cost.
options.why: Swaps the two definitions; consumer surplus uses buyers' willingness to pay and producer surplus uses sellers' costs.

options.text: Producer surplus is the difference between the price sellers receive and their minimum acceptable price, while consumer surplus is the difference between buyers' maximum willingness to pay and the price paid.
options.why: Both are net gains from trade measured against the market price, one for sellers and one for buyers.

options.text: Producer surplus is the area above the supply curve and below the demand curve, which is the same as consumer surplus.
options.why: Describes total surplus; each surplus is a separate triangle bounded by the price line.

options.text: Both surpluses equal zero at the equilibrium, because the market clears there.
options.why: Confuses market clearing with zero gains; only the marginal unit has zero surplus.

payload.stem: The government imposes a per-unit tax on coffee. In this market the absolute value of the price elasticity of demand is 2.0 and the price elasticity of supply is 1.0. Which of the following best describes the burden of the tax?

options.text: Sellers bear the entire tax, because they remit it to the government.
options.why: Equates the party that pays the government with the party that bears the burden.

options.text: Producers bear the larger share, because supply is less elastic than demand.
options.why: The side of the market that is less elastic is less able to avoid the tax, so it bears the larger share of the burden.

options.text: The burden depends only on the size of the tax and not on elasticities.
options.why: Ignores that elasticities determine how the burden is shared.

options.text: Consumers and producers bear equal shares, because the tax is collected from sellers.
options.why: Believes the legal incidence determines the economic incidence.

options.text: Consumers bear the larger share, because demand is less elastic than supply.
options.why: Reverses the rule: the more elastic side can avoid the tax, so the more inelastic side bears more.

payload.stem: The government imposes a per-unit tax on orange juice. In this market the absolute value of the price elasticity of demand is 3.0 and the price elasticity of supply is 1.0. Which of the following best describes the burden of the tax?

options.text: Consumers bear the entire tax, because the price rises by the amount of the tax.
options.why: Assumes the price always rises by the full tax.

options.text: Producers bear the larger share, because supply is less elastic than demand.
options.why: The side of the market that is less elastic is less able to avoid the tax, so it bears the larger share of the burden.

options.text: Consumers bear the larger share, because demand is less elastic than supply.
options.why: Reverses the rule: the more elastic side can avoid the tax, so the more inelastic side bears more.

options.text: Consumers and producers bear equal shares, because the tax is collected from sellers.
options.why: Believes the legal incidence determines the economic incidence.

options.text: Sellers bear the entire tax, because they remit it to the government.
options.why: Equates the party that pays the government with the party that bears the burden.
